questions.def: Nominal relative clauses use 'what' to refer to the thing mentioned.
questions.question: ___ he told me was a complete surprise.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a nominal relative clause functioning as the object.
questions.question: I didn't understand ___ the speaker was referring to.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause that acts as the subject.
questions.question: ___ she said is hard to accept.

questions.def: 'What' refers to the company, acting as the subject.
questions.question: She invested in ___ seemed like a promising startup.

questions.def: 'Whatever' means anything that you decide.
questions.question: ___ you decide is fine with me.

questions.def: Use 'whom' as the object of 'decides' in this nominal clause.
questions.question: Who he decides to hire is ultimately his decision.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause acting as the direct object.
questions.question: I gave him ___ he needed.

questions.def: 'What' begins a nominal relative clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ I'm concerned about is the long-term impact.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause, the object of understood.
questions.question: He finally understood ___ she meant.

questions.def: Use 'what' instead of 'that' to introduce the nominal relative clause.
questions.question: That she said was quite different than expected.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ happened next was unbelievable.

questions.def: 'Whatever' means anything she decides to do.
questions.question: ___ she decides to do is her own business.

questions.def: 'Whoever' acts as the subject of the verb 'asks'.
questions.question: I'll give it to ___ asks first.

questions.def: The subject should be introduced by 'that' not 'what'.
questions.question: What he didn't know is that she was lying.

questions.def: 'Whatever' means anything that you choose.
questions.question: ___ you choose will be fine with me.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ is important is that we remain calm.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the nominal relative clause.
questions.question: ___ he said surprised everyone in the room.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause, the object of 'accepted'.
questions.question: He accepted ___ was offered.

questions.def: 'What' functions as the subject complement.
questions.question: She wants ___ is best for her children.

questions.def: 'What' functions as the direct object of 'gave'.
questions.question: He gave ___ he had to charity.

questions.def: Use 'whom' as the object of 'told' in this nominal clause.
questions.question: Who she told was supposed to be a secret.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause as the subject.
questions.question: ___ you decide will affect us all.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause as the subject.
questions.question: ___ I dislike most is his arrogance.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause as the complement.
questions.question: That's exactly ___ I mean.

questions.def: The sentence is gramatically correct. No error.
questions.question: That is what makes him happy.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause as the object.
questions.question: I followed ___ he recommended.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause as the subject.
questions.question: ___ she told me was confidential.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause as the object of the preposition.
questions.question: I'm interested in ___ you have to say.

questions.def: "What" introduces a nominal relative clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ she said surprised everyone in the room.

questions.def: "What" is correct as a nominal relative clause functioning as an object.
questions.question: I couldn't believe ___ happened during the meeting.
